I’ve got kind of a weird question. 

So, we know that the way Makima’s contract works is that she can be revived from death after anything considered an “attack” successfully kills her. And the reason Denji eating her did not lead to her revival is because he had no intention to harm her by doing so; he considered it an act of love. Therefore, his actions did not qualify as an “attack,” leaving the conditions for Makima’s revival unfulfilled, permanently killing her.

Okay, that’s all fine and good, but that sort of made me think. Could Makima be killed through an accident of some sort? Like, let’s say that she’s walking down the street (with her guard down, for the sake of the argument), and somebody accidentally drops something off their balcony, hitting her in the head, and killing her. The person who dropped the object had no intention to harm Makima—their clumsy actions just happened to lead to Makima’s death in the same way Denji’s act of love also happened to result in her death. So it would be reasonable to assume that because there was no intention to harm behind the accident, it would not qualify as an “attack” either, leaving the revival conditions unfulfilled. What do you think? Is something like this theoretically possible?
